bull.b: Sustained high gross margins and favorable per‑unit cash economics indicate the product can scale profitably once adoption improves. Durable unit economics lower the revenue threshold to breakeven, support attractive LTV/CAC dynamics if refill persistence holds, and make future margin expansion feasible.

bull.t: Growing prescriber base and script traction
bull.b: A large and expanding prescriber base with meaningful script volume demonstrates durable commercial penetration and physician acceptance. Repeated prescribing by many clinicians suggests a foundation for sustained uptake and lower marginal customer acquisition costs as field efforts and e‑pharmacy channels scale.

bull.t: Conservative balance sheet with meaningful cash
bull.b: A strong cash position and negligible leverage provide runway to execute the early commercial plan and invest in marketing without immediate refinancing. Conservative capitalization reduces solvency risk, allowing management time to prove refill economics and scale revenues before capital markets pressure mounts.

bear.b: Material and continuing negative operating and free cash flows mean the company depends on external financing to fund operations. This creates dilution and execution risk if commercial adoption lags, and limits flexibility to increase or sustain promotional investment without replenishing cash resources via markets or partners.

bear.t: High SG&A and front‑loaded launch costs
bear.b: Elevated fixed selling and marketing costs compress operating leverage and extend the time to breakeven unless revenue scales rapidly. Front‑loaded DTC and field investments raise the break‑even revenue requirement and increase cash burn vulnerability if physician conversion and patient refills take longer than anticipated.

Eliminating near‑term R&D preserves cash for commercialization but reduces pipeline optionality and long‑term product diversification. If the current launch faces competitive or safety setbacks, the lack of active development programs limits strategic alternatives and makes the company reliant on a single commercial asset.
